reviews.title: Two Years of Training Data. Still Doing the Programming Myself.
reviews.text:
I’ve been subscribed to Fitbod since 2024, yet I still do virtually all the workout programming myself. Despite extensive training history, exercise substitutions, preferences, and corrections, I routinely rebuild its recommendations rather than follow them.

The Beta Coach mostly points out the obvious like identifying the element of an upcoming workout instead of delivering actionable insights. Progress reports emphasize activity totals while overlooking meaningful strength progression and exercise-specific personal records. 

I continue subscribing primarily for strength scores and my workout history data (baselines/ records), not personalized programming. These tracking features alone hardly justify premium pricing when the app’s core functionality still requires extensive manual intervention.

Fitbod claims its AI learns from training and workout adjustments to deliver personalized programming. After more than two year of providing both, why am I still doing virtually all the programming myself and what actually justifies $96 annually?

reviews.title: I want so badly to like this app
reviews.text: I'm not new to lifting, but I rely on apps like this for guidance. Earlier this year I used Fitbod consistently and built up to a solid weight. Then life happened, and I started having multiple weeks between sessions. The AI coach would say "I see you've been gone for a month," and then the first workout back would be a "max effort day" at or above my peak weight. It recognizes I've been away, and instead of a gradual reintroduction, it puts me in a position to get injured. I'm shocked the app expects me to lower the weights myself after time off. That's exactly what I'm paying it to do! Adapting to real life fluctuations is the feature that should justify the price.

reviews.title: It’s ok
reviews.text:
While this app is ok for beginners, kind of, there are some glaringly obvious negatives which the team must be aware of and ignoring. The progression is all over the place, it regularly expects you to be able to do double (in either weight or sets) from the previous workout, which means taking time to go through and adjusting every workout in advance or taking time out of your workout to stand in the gym fiddling with the app. 
The new AI “coach” is pointless, it just takes up space on the screen to give you a generic sentence. 
Second is the cost, it is hideously expensive for what it is and the new family plan just rubs it in even more. I’d love to be able to get the family plan so my husband can use it too but only having the option to pay yearly is rubbish. The company have made it very clear they just want to rinse customers for as much money as possible and it’s just scummy behaviour. 
This app could be so much better if they just listened to customer feedback and actually implemented it rather than just giving a corporate type “we’re working on it” response. Like the fix for workouts syncing twice to Apple, that was posted about on Reddit 6 months ago and apparently the fix was “in review and will be coming soon, hopefully by the end of this week!” - it’s still not fixed.

reviews.title: Not good anymore
reviews.text: I’ve had this app for many years and for the most part have loved it and think it really is the best app out there in terms of how customizable it is and the UI being excellent. The format with the video demos and the way you can customize workouts by selecting muscle grooves among other things is great too, but the thing that really made me decide to finally cancel my subscription is the fact that it just kept giving me the same workouts every single day with no variation, despite selecting increased variability in the options for the workouts. Additionally, when I select certain muscle groups together, it’ll come back and tell me it can’t generate a workout, which makes no sense physiologically. I’ve contacted customer support about this, but just haven’t come up with any kind of solution. Also, they severely increased their prices and I just don’t think it’s competitive or worth it anymore. I’ve also noticed that, despite telling the app to increase inclusion of certain exercises more often it still doesn’t do it, for example, the pullover is never recommended in any of my workouts, despite this being an awesome movement for me. I have to manually add it every single time. Still I have yet to find a better workout app out there. But I can’t justify paying for this app anymore.

reviews.title: Final update: I no longer subscribe.
reviews.text:
Update to update: An app update earlier this year really destroyed the progressive workouts the app gave me. It started suggesting weird stuff. I tried changing settings, I spoke at length to customer service. I even deleted and reloaded the app, which messed up my Apple settings. Nothing took the workouts back to what was working for me. I have moved on to Gravl which I am already liking much more. For one, the timer does not cut my music off. The app also asked a series of questions to get to know my experience and goals and programs workout that are consistent with my feedback. Pricing is competitive with Fitbod.

Previous Update: I don’t think any of my past suggestions have been implemented. Been using this app almost a year, previously gave it 4 stars as some improvements are needed. The latest update has made me remove another star. It’s really messed up my programming. Even choosing more consistent exercises, it is giving me a weird workout. So I have to spend time undoing and redoing it all. Time programming is the main reason I chose an app. I’m considering the RP Hypertrophy app as it might be more aligned with my goals. This app is ok for a beginner or casual exerciser, but it’s a real hassle if you want to program progressive workout.
